title: Sterling Bose, Pollock and a road trip with Earl Crum
summary: Hirsch recalls Sterling Bose, a trip north with Earl Crum and his wife where they saw Pollock in Detroit, and the 1933 World's Fair.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: No, no, no, no. You're thinking of, uh, of, uh, Pollock.

Pollock. Pollock. That's what I mean. And he was, uh, he was with that band. In fact, I saw him in, out of Detroit. They were at some nightclub up there. Uh, and that's when Earl Crum and Franklin, Earl's wife and I were making a trip. We went up to, uh, Chicago and all through Minneapolis and went over to, to, uh, Canada. Back down to Pittsburgh, back all the way down here. And, uh, we saw, we saw that, uh, up there.
Uh, but, uh, it was. Was that when you went to the World's Fair or another time?
Oh, you might have been sure.
That was another. The World's Fair was in 1933.
